_comment: Elder Rowan conversations. DialogueDB picks the FIRST entry whose 'requires' match (most specific must come first). Flag '<quest>_<objective>' is auto-raised when that objective completes.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: Grey flecks on the washing-line. Rowan says it is not woodsmoke, and he wants the slimes thinned before the village starts asking questions.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Slay 4 Slime Grunt. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: The tanner pays in coin for slime gel, and Rowan wants the stores full before the frost turns.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Gather 3 Slime Gel. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: Something is raising Millhaven's dead badly -- as if it had learned how from a book, not a rite. Put them down.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Slay 6 Rotting Husk. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: The glands in the husks are wrong for corpses this fresh. Rowan wants them on his table before the smell decides anything.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Gather 4 Fetid Gland. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: A sealed writ arrives from Sunreach City. Rowan does not open it; he says the seal is on the inside.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Reach Visited Sunreach. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: The warrens are breathing. Every emberling you leave is a lungful of the thing coming up the road.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Slay 8 Emberling. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: Six embers, sealed and boxed, for the road wardens' braziers.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Gather 6 Emberling Ember. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: Rowan finally opens the writ. Sunreach is sending someone east, and the road east does not stay in the Meadows.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Speak with Old Rowan. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Old Rowan
1.text: You climb back into the snow at the scorched ring with the ledger, the shards and the word 'vessel' in your mouth. Rowan is waiting at the edge of the burn, and he already knows what you are going to say.

2.speaker: Old Rowan
2.text: Speak with Old Rowan. Come back to me when it is done.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: The road is safer now, thanks to you. Stay as long as you like, friend.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: It is done, then... and you chose mercy over vengeance. The Warden was once our guardian — corrupted by my old mistake.

2.speaker: Elder Rowan
2.text: You gave it peace instead of fury. Perhaps that is how all of us hope to be remembered.

3.speaker: Elder Rowan
3.text: Take this ring, traveler. It belonged to the Warden in better days. May it carry you far.

4.speaker: Elder Rowan
4.text: What do we do with what the Warden told you? Say it and it becomes a thing the valley has to carry. Keep it and it stays a thing you carry alone.

choices.text: Bury it. Let the valley heal without it.
I will carry it. Somebody should know.

5.speaker: Elder Rowan
5.text: Then it goes in the burn, deep enough that the next person has to dig for it. Some answers are only useful to the person who earns them.

6.speaker: Elder Rowan
6.text: Then carry it, and let the road hear it. Better a hard thing said out loud than a hard thing kept in a pocket.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: It is done. You burned the corruption out root and branch — just as you swore.

2.speaker: Elder Rowan
2.text: Part of me mourns the guardian it once was. But the living come first, and you chose them.

3.speaker: Elder Rowan
3.text: Take this blade. It has waited long for a hand steady enough to wield it.

4.speaker: Elder Rowan
4.text: What do we do with what the Warden told you? Say it and it becomes a thing the valley has to carry. Keep it and it stays a thing you carry alone.

choices.text: Bury it. Let the valley heal without it.
I will carry it. Somebody should know.

5.speaker: Elder Rowan
5.text: Then it goes in the burn, deep enough that the next person has to dig for it. Some answers are only useful to the person who earns them.

6.speaker: Elder Rowan
6.text: Then carry it, and let the road hear it. Better a hard thing said out loud than a hard thing kept in a pocket.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: The Warden waits at the scorched ring, northeast of here. Watch for the gold glow before it strikes — that's your window to roll aside.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: You saw the ring... then you saw the truth I have carried for thirty years.

2.speaker: Elder Rowan
2.text: The Warden was this valley's guardian. I tried to bind more power into it than flesh could hold. The fire you saw is my failure, given form.

3.speaker: Elder Rowan
3.text: It must be stopped. But how you face it... that choice is yours, not mine.

4.speaker: Elder Rowan
4.text: How will you face the Warden?

choices.text: With vengeance. It burned everything I love.
With mercy. It is a victim too.

5v.speaker: Elder Rowan
5v.text: Then may your arm be as sure as your heart is set. End it.

5m.speaker: Elder Rowan
5m.text: Mercy... yes. Perhaps it deserves that much. Free it from the flame.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: Northeast, past the barrens, the ground itself is scorched into a perfect ring. Nothing grows there. Nothing sleeps there.

2.speaker: Elder Rowan
2.text: Go. See it with your own eyes. Then come back to me — you deserve the truth of it.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: You've done it — the camp can breathe again. You fight like someone the road has sharpened.

2.speaker: Elder Rowan
2.text: Take this coin. And traveler... there is something darker stirring in the northeast. I need your eyes on it.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: The slimes still prowl just beyond the firelight. Watch for their wind-up glow before they lunge — that's your cue to roll aside.

1.speaker: Elder Rowan
1.text: Ah — a new face on the road. Welcome to our little fire, traveler. I am Rowan, elder of what's left of this camp.

2.speaker: Elder Rowan
2.text: You arrive at a poor hour. Slimes have grown bold and crept right up to our walls. My knees are too old for blades.

3.speaker: Elder Rowan
3.text: Would you thin them out for us? Three of the brutes should send the rest packing.

choices.text: Why should I risk my neck?

3b.speaker: Elder Rowan
3b.text: Fair. Coin, then — and my thanks when it's done. We take care of those who take care of us.

4.speaker: Elder Rowan
4.text: They prowl just outside the firelight. And traveler — roll aside when they glow. They always lunge after.

barks.text: The camp fire never goes out. Small mercies.
Millhaven has stood through three winters like this one. Stand, or fall — that is all the world asks.
You have your mother's stubbornness. Use it.
Sleep while you can. The night has grown louder.
